summary: Jan Nattier is a scholar of Buddhist, Sinological, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Indiana University Bloomington and Harvard University (PhD under Masatoshi Nagatomi), later holding professorships at Indiana University Bloomington (1992–2005) and Soka University (2004–2010).

Jan P. Hogendijk is a historian and Indologist who earned his doctorate from Utrecht University in 1983. He held professorships in the history of mathematics at Utrecht University (2005) and Leiden University (2004–2009).

Jan Peter F. Hintelmann is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Marianne Pieper and studied under several traditional teachers.

Jan Van Bragt (1928–2007) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at KU Leuven from around 1948 to 1957 and served as Director at Nanzan University (~1976–1992), where he was later named professor emeritus.

Jan Westerhoff is a philosopher and Indologist specializing in Buddhist studies. He earned PhDs from the University of Cambridge under Michael Potter and SOAS University of London. He became Professor of Buddhist Philosophy at the University of Oxford around 2012.

Jan Willem de Jong (1921–2000) was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Leiden University, where he held the Chair of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies (1950–1956) before heading South Asian and Buddhist Studies at ANU (1965–1986).

Jan-Ulrich Sobisch specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under David P. Jackson, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Nubpa Rinpoche, and he served as a professor at the University of Copenhagen (2003–2006).
Jane Bunnag is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of London in 1969, where she studied under supervisors Nathaniel Tarn and Barbara E. Ward.
Jane Caple works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at the University of Leeds and at the University of Manchester, where she is attested as a Research Fellow in 2026.

Jane Ellen Harrison (1850–1928) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. She studied at Cheltenham Ladies' College, Newnham College, and under Robert Alexander Neil, and held a post at the University of Cambridge from roughly 1898 to 1922.
Jane-Marie Law works in Japanology and religious studies. She has served at Cornell University as Director of Graduate Studies (attested 2008) and as Associate Professor (attested 2026).

Janet Gyatso is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who earned her BA, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley. She taught at Amherst College (1987–2001) and became the Hershey Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard Divinity School in 2001.
Jang-Kil Chun specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chun studied under Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Frances Wilson, and doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota.

Janice Dean Willis is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD in Indic and Buddhist Studies at Columbia University under Alex Wayman and served as a professor at Wesleyan University from 1977 to 2013.

Janice Leoshko specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her doctoral studies under Susan L. Huntington and is attested as Professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin in 2026.

Jann Ronis is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisor David Germano and teacher Jeffrey Hopkins, and held an affiliation there attested in 2007.

Jared Rhoton (1941–1992) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga and completed his doctoral dissertation at Columbia University under Alex Wayman by 1985.

Jarl Charpentier (1884–1935) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Bonn and Uppsala University (PhD 1908) under Hermann Jacobi and Karl Ferdinand Johansson, whom he succeeded as professor at Uppsala in 1927.
Jaroslav Průšek (1906–1980) was a Sinologist. He completed his studies at Charles University's Faculty of Arts in Prague between approximately 1924 and 1928.

Jason Birch is an Indologist who studied at the University of Sydney and earned his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (2013) under Alexis Sanderson. He was a postdoctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).
